one_provider_refusal_then_successes.cause: The harness ignores .category (it did not exist in v3) and keyword-classifies the message. The v4 provider_refusal message itself contains the word budget twice ('Other budget may remain; check budget.remaining().'), and _classify_error (harness.py lines 186-206) tests 'budget' (line 192) before 'refus' (line 198). The loop then returns at lines 681-683 without calling budget.remaining().

verdict_rationale: On platform v4 the frozen H0 v3 still ends the action loop after a single provider refusal while budget remains, the failure class that invalidated integration v1. All other interface behaviour matches the previous review (schemas valid and free of reasoning requests, capability grants, budgets, cancellation, manifest, state reset), and genuine budget exhaustion correctly stops the loop. The H0 must not be patched by maintainers.
options_for_root: Platform: make every non-budget_exhausted public message free of the word 'budget' (consistent with the stated intent that only budget_exhausted signals exhaustion; the v4 docs and .category already tell harnesses to use remaining()). In the v3 review a refusal message without budget keywords took the harness's continue path (N2_TYPED_REFUSAL: 4 act steps, completed). This changes an ABI-visible message for all harnesses, needs a version note, and must be re-verified with the exact new text; note the risk of appearing to tune platform wording to one harness's keyword heuristic - the justification should be the general ambiguity, stated before re-testing.
Rebuild H0 against interface v4 (which exposes .category).
Run integration anyway with V3-1 recorded as a known H0 property and treat any post-refusal early stop as a non-measurement.
limitations: Fake clients only; the real ExecutorBroker/ContainerExecutor/ClaudeJSONTransport and literature service were not run.
